# A disposal that balances its residual onto the bank and states the gain.
#
# `$residual$` is a balancing feature, not a currency one: it writes on any
# account whose commodity is the transaction's. So a file may let the bank take
# what is left over — 1,400.00, what the dollars fetched — and say on the income
# line which split is the exchange difference.
#
# One split claims the difference, not two. A residual balancing onto a bank
# moved money rather than measuring anything, and neither the import's mark nor
# the page's reading counts it, so counting it as a *claim* refused this file
# as claiming twice what it claims once — and left no way to have the gain
# counted at all short of working the bank figure out by hand.
#
# So it imports, and the page states the 100.00 the sale made.
#
# `{usd_basis}` is the guid of the purchase's cost basis, read from
# `fx-balances` after the first import.
2026-06-01 * "Sell every dollar at 1.40"
	currency.mnemonic: "CAD"
	Assets:USD Bank -1000.00 USD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
		share_price: "13/10"
		value: "-1300.00"
		cost_basis_split_guid: "{usd_basis}"
	Assets:CAD Bank $residual$ CAD
	Income:FX Gain -100.00 CAD
		took_the_residual: "true"
